ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, shareholders, and individuals with significant control against the following standards: (1) Canadian sanctions lists issued under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA) and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (2) United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions adopted under the United Nations Act; (3) OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, mandatory given the intended USD-denominated Stripe and Escrow payment rails; (4) UK and EU consolidated sanctions lists as a prudent cross-jurisdictional overlay; and (5) determination of Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status under PCMLTFA section 11.1 and FINTRAC guidance, with enhanced due diligence mandated for foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates, given the vintage luxury resale sector's Medium_Risk_Enhanced banking profile.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry - Corporate Access (CORES) online system operated by Service Alberta and accessed through authorized Corporate Registry service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English, French, or a combination of both; names originating in non-Latin scripts require a certified English or French transliteration or translation filed with the registry. The name must be clearly distinguishable from all existing names appearing in the Alberta corporate registry and NUANS name search reports, must not be misleading with respect to the corporate identity, and must comply with the distinguishing-number and legal element requirements of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Institute (where implying a post-secondary educational institution)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the Alberta Corporate Registry issues a notice of refusal under section 12 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Director of Corporate Registry within the response period stated in the refusal notice. The submission must distinguish the proposed name from the conflicting trademarks or registered business names, provide supporting branding, trademark search, and goodwill evidence, and may propose minor amendments. The Director renders a written decision; if the refusal is upheld, the applicant may incorporate under an acceptable alternative name or file a change-of-name application, and ultimately may seek judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta within the applicable limitation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the statutory registered office. Alberta law requires a physical street address within Alberta where process may be served and where the corporate records and the Individual with Significant Control (ISC) register are retained and available for inspection. A virtual mailbox or virtual office may be used only for supplementary operational correspondence and cannot discharge the statutory registered office obligation for this e-commerce business corporation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by Alberta Corporate Registry is assessed at approximately 5% for a low-capital service corporation; however, the likelihood of a FINTRAC compliance examination or provincial consumer-protection audit rises to approximately 20-30% within the first 24 months of operation once card-present or card-not-present payment processing via Stripe and Escrow rails commences in the secondhand luxury goods vertical.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9, Part 2 (Sections 2-1 to 2-9) - Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; shares may be issued for nominal or nil value consideration
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Articles of Incorporation of [Entity Name] be approved and filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry pursuant to the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), establishing the corporation with [number] authorized common shares having a par value of $1.00 each. RESOLVED THAT [Director Name] be appointed as the first director of the corporation, responsible for executing all incorporation documents and initial share subscriptions. RESOLVED THAT the registered office of the corporation be located at [Alberta address], and that the incorporator [Incorp Name] subscribe for all initial shares. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the incorporator is authorized to submit the filing, pay the statutory fee, and complete all post-incorporation filings to obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform name search on the Alberta Corporate Registry website to ensure the proposed name is available; if available, submit the name reservation form online or by mail with any required fee; obtain confirmation of reservation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is unavailable, select an alternative name and repeat the search process within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation using the prescribed form, including details on share classes, directors, and registered office; upload the completed form and supporting documents to the online portal; remit the filing fee of $100 CAD; await electronic confirmation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, provide additional information or resubmit corrected documents within the prescribed timeframe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Receive the Certificate of Incorporation via email or mail; update the corporation's internal records; file any required notices with other government agencies such as CRA for tax identification; commence business operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request an extension or appeal if processing exceeds SLA by contacting the registry directly.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA); Business Registration Online and My Business Account portal at www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes.html, with GST/HST NETFILE filing and BN (Business Number) issuance via the central registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Canadian-incorporated Business Corporation obtains its 9-digit BN automatically through the corporate registry (Federal Corporations Canada or Alberta Corporate Registry via ABConnect). The BN is activated for income tax upon incorporation and for GST/HST by filing Form RC1A or through Business Registration Online (BRO). A foreign-entity seller without a Canadian incorporation files Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) with CRA, designating the GST/HST program (RT) and providing evidence of foreign registration, a Canadian address for service or authorized representative, and a description of the Canadian commercial activity; non-resident sellers may also apply electronically under the simplified GST/HST non-resident registration module before effecting taxable supplies in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Inc./Corp. is a separate taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act; it is not pass-through, and all income is computed and taxed at the corporate level before any dividend distribution, with Alberta corporate income tax levied on the same taxable income. No territorial election is available for this structure; Canadian-resident corporations are taxed on worldwide income, while capital-gains and foreign-affiliate rules apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No United-States-style check-the-box election exists. Relevant Canadian elections for this cross-border resale structure include: (i) the GST/HST closely related corporation election under section 150 of the Excise Tax Act to treat taxable supplies among related group members as non-supplies; (ii) the section 216 election permitting a non-resident corporation to compute Canadian-source rental or timber income on a net basis; (iii) the section 219 deemed non-resident taxation election for Canadian subsidiaries of foreign parents and associated surplus-dividend elections under subsection 112(1); (iv) optional streamlined GST/HST registration and non-resident rebate elections (e.g., public service body rebate equivalents) for the foreign vendor; and (v) hybrid-mismatch alignment elections and documentation for fiscally transparent foreign entities (including US LLCs) under the hybrid mismatch rules of the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) — a federal value-added tax administered by the CRA; Alberta participates with 0% provincial component and no provincial sales tax, yielding an effective 5% GST rate only.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated supplies and financial services) in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; exceeding the threshold mandates registration and remittance. For non-resident sellers of tangible personal property (including secondhand luxury goods) facilitated through a distribution platform deemed to be the supplier, the platform operator bears registration and collection duties, and the foreign seller is exempt from GST/HST registration for those platform-facilitated supplies. Direct sales by the foreign vendor to Canadian consumers outside a platform, or importations of goods for local resale, attract the standard threshold and separate import GST obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose a real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory digital stamping, or API-based invoice clearance regime at the federal level. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically through GST/HST NETFILE when annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 1.5 million or in all cases for newly registered bank/credit-union cases; electronic remittance is compulsory for registrants with monthly or quarterly reporting. The CRA is a participant in the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework and the PEPPOL network, requiring PEPPOL e-invoices for federal B2G procurement; additionally, Revenu Québec mandates EDI (e.g., ANSI X12 or EDIFACT) or equivalent electronic invoicing for selected large suppliers and for certain B2B transactions in Quebec. No digital stamping or prior approval of invoices exists for B2C e-commerce export resale.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act, supplies of tangible personal property delivered by the vendor (or by the purchaser taking the goods abroad) to an address outside Canada are zero-rated at export. Eligible vintage-luxury resale items (handbags, watches, jewellery, collectibles and apparel) qualify when: (i) the online vendor ships or delivers the goods directly to a non-resident buyer outside Canada; (ii) title and risk of loss pass to the non-resident buyer; and (iii) export occurs as soon as reasonably practicable (CRA administrative practice generally requiring export within 60 days of sale). Services supplied to a non-resident that are performed entirely outside Canada, or that directly relate to goods situated outside Canada at the time of supply (e.g., sourcing/consignment agent services for an offshore seller), may also be zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration: Canada Customs B13A Export Declaration (or authorized customs broker export report) filed with CBSA via the Canadian Economic Development Agency or the Export Reporting System, identifying the goods, value, and destination country.

Bill of Lading or International Transport Evidence: ocean Bill of Lading, airway bill, or postal/courier waybill (Canada Post, FedEx, UPS) with complete tracking data and customs release stamps showing delivery to an address outside Canada within the export window.

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC): bank-issued documentary evidence of foreign-currency settlement (SWIFT MT103 or escrow/payment processor settlement ledger from Stripe or Escrow Pay) demonstrating receipt of payment from the non-resident buyer and matching the invoice, foreign currency, and invoice amount.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is a high-risk audit profile for the CRA. In the absence of a valid B13A, transport document, and IRC, the CRA disallows the 0% rate, reassesses the sale at 5% GST with compounding daily arrears interest, and extends the normal four-year reassessment window indefinitely where the taxpayer has made a misrepresentation. Civil penalties include a failure-to-file penalty of 1% of the unreported net tax plus 25% on repeated failures, a 'gravely negligent' penalty of 25% of the net tax avoided under section 285 of the Excise Tax Act, and denial of refunds. Knowingly creating fraudulent export declarations (fabricated bills of lading, simulated shipments, sham consignment partners) constitutes an offence under section 327, punishable by fines up to CAD 25,000 and imprisonment for up to five years; CRA may also publicly name and debar offenders, seize bank accounts, and apply the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) to transaction recharacterization.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with foreign-exchange administration duties shared by the Department of Finance Canada and prudential reporting to the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); transaction monitoring and cross-border currency-flow reporting are enforced by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a free-floating Canadian dollar with unrestricted convertibility on both current account and capital account. No exchange controls, no capital-transfer approvals, and no profit-remittance restrictions exist for a federally incorporated Alberta business. Dividends to non-resident shareholders are subject to Part XIII withholding tax (generally 25%, treaty-reduced to 5-15% depending on recipient jurisdiction), but remittance itself is unencumbered. Statutory institutional constraints are limited to FINTRAC reporting on CAD 10,000+ international electronic funds transfers and, where non-resident investors acquire control, Investment Canada Act notification/review thresholds. This enables the luxury-resale treasury to hold USD/EUR proceeds in segregated accounts and to pay consignors freely.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No Canadian exchange-control law imposes export-proceeds surrender; there is no statutory timeline and no required conversion ratio. Vintage luxury resale exports may be settled and retained in USD, EUR, or any freely convertible currency. The only binding obligation is the PCMLTFA duty on financial institutions to report international EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more, and the corporate obligation to keep full invoice, customs, authentication, and payment records for seven years for CRA and OSFI audit verification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a regional settlement accelerator, but Low as a primary treasury rail. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise Business, Airwallex, Revolut Business) are not authorized under the Bank Act to accept demand deposits and cannot provide the regulatory stack required for FINTRAC-compliant corporate treasury in Alberta. A Canadian-controlled private corporation may use an EMI solely as a collection gateway for low-margin, low-UK/Europe corridors, provided the main Canada bank is disclosed, the EMI never holds capital-escrow balances, and transaction volumes remain below CAD 25,000 per payment. Legal constraint: any hold of CAD customer funds by an unlicensed EMI triggers a compliance breach and may cause the charter bank to de-risk the primary account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: All Schedule I banks require an in-person KYC interview at an Alberta branch for at least one director, officer, or authorised signatory before opening a business account for a newly incorporated cross-border luxury resale company. Remote video verification is available only after the physical relationship is established, or for subsequent signatories. Non-resident directors may delegate their meeting to a Canadian-resident signatory holding a notarized power of attorney, but the bank must still review original certified passports, corporate resolutions, registered-agent confirmation, and beneficial-ownership declarations. For enhanced-risk files, an initial physical interview is not waived in practice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent collection flow where Stripe and Escrow_Pay settle large batches to the corporate account, creating unclear beneficial ownership at counterparty level.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a payment-system data map, monthly merchant settlement statements from both processors, escrow trust account attestation, refund and dispute history, and a documented customer-identification framework; state in the treasury policy that processors are only collection agents, and provide the bank with live read-only account access to validate settlement provenance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border sourcing of luxury pre-owned stock from private collectors, estate liquidations, or jurisdictions with weak AML frameworks, raising suspicion of stolen or laundered goods.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a per-item provenance pack: original or restoration invoice, notarised consignment agreement, independent authentication firm report (Entrupy, Real Authentication, or auction-house certificate), macro-photography of serial numbers/hallmarks, condition report, and a chain-of-custody log from intake to dispatch; include supplier completed KYC questionaires and sanctioned-party screening results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value customer order (above CAD 10,000) diverted to a third-party address or a freight-forwarder, indicating possible goods trafficking or unregulated export.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Retain verified buyer identity (government photo ID, matching payment card/Escrow_Pay verification, IP and device fingerprint), commercial invoice, HS classification, courier airway bill, shipment insurance, and the company's board-approved red-flag escalation policy; secure second-level approval from a designated compliance officer and document FINTRAC reporting context if an international transfer is involved.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident investor to the Alberta subsidiary's operating or capital account, with a clear purpose code and narrative: 'EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION – CBCA CORPORATE ACT' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN – TREASURY SUPPORT'. No Bank of Canada or FINTRAC pre-approval is required, but the receiving bank will ask for a board resolution, updated corporate register, beneficial-ownership form, source-of-funds evidence for sums exceeding CAD 50,000, and a completed Investment Canada Act notification if applicable. Settle CAD through LVTS or Payments Canada Real-Time Rail; settle USD through the bank's New York correspondent via Fedwire/CHIPS. All inward transfers above CAD 10,000 are automatically reported by the financial institution to FINTRAC as International Electronic Funds Transfers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disburse to foreign consignors/suppliers via SWIFT MT103 with invoice references, incoterms and 'LUXURY RESALE INVENTORY' purpose narrative. Domestic payouts use Payments Canada EFT or Interac e-Transfer; settlement to Escrow_Pay uses standard ACH/EFT rails. For large replenishment purchases from accredited distributors, issue a sight commercial letter of credit (MT700) payable against presentation of transport documents, commercial invoices, and an authentication certificate. To avoid double-clearing, ensure the FX conversion happens at a single Schedule I bank and that all payouts reconcile against the escrow/processors' trust ledger.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable USD/CAD forward contracts and FX swaps transacted under an ISDA Master Agreement with a Schedule I Canadian bank for treasury hedging of USD-denominated resale inventory — NDFs are not permissible because CAD is a fully convertible deliverable currency
Exchange-traded USD/CAD and EUR/CAD futures and options on the Montreal Exchange (MX) / Cboe Canada, limited to documented hedging of committed luxury-goods purchases
Vanilla USD/CAD currency options and zero-cost collars with tenors up to 12 months, aligned with projected revenue conversion requirements
Cross-currency interest-rate basis swaps for long-term USD borrowings used to finance cross-border inventory acquisitions, subject to the corporation's board-approved derivative-risk policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default for two consecutive annual filing years may lead to administrative dissolution by the Director; all outstanding annual returns must be filed before reinstatement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the day six months after the corporation's taxation year-end; June 30 for a calendar-year corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; repeat non-filers face 10% plus 2% per complete month up to 20 months; daily compound interest on arrears at prescribed CRA rates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and interest apply to Alberta corporate income tax payable under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act; assessed and administered through the CRA tax administration agreement

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, an independent auditor must be appointed unless all shareholders, including non-voting shareholders, unanimously consent annually to waive the auditor. A distributing corporation may not use the waiver. No revenue, asset, or employee size threshold applies for a private Alberta corporation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises; private enterprises may elect either IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under the CPA Canada Handbook. Tax returns are reconciled to taxable income under the federal Income Tax Act and Alberta Corporate Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not impose a separate annual UBO re-filing for private non-distributing corporations. The register of members and register of transfers must be updated immediately on each share transfer and be available for statutory review. If the entity is a CBCA corporation, the federal annual return to Corporations Canada requires annual confirmation of individuals with significant control; in all cases, any change in significant control must be recorded in the corporation's significant-control register within 30 days of knowledge.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000–35,000 depending on transaction volume, inventory valuation, and e-commerce payment complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined federal-plus-Alberta general corporate rate (Federal Part I 15.0% + Alberta 8.0%); 11.0% combined federal-plus-Alberta rate on the first CA$500,000 of active business income for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPC) claiming the small business deduction (Federal 9.0% + Alberta 2.0%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays for luxury resale/trading entities. Preferential measures: (i) small business deduction (SBD) reducing combined federal-provincial rate to 11% on first CA$500,000 of active business income; (ii) refundable SR&ED investment tax credits (35% for qualifying CCPCs) on eligible scientific research and experimental development expenditures; (iii) accelerated capital cost allowance and immediate expensing for certain digitalized e-commerce equipment and software; (iv) Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax, no capital tax, and no payroll tax for employers.
